title: Good Copy
subtitle: The Roomy Amateur Radio Logbook: 1,320 Contacts with Large Writing Space, POTA / SOTA, Contest and Net Logs, WAS, DXCC and Grid Trackers, Band and Q-Code Reference
categories: Crafts, Hobbies & Home > Antiques & Collectibles > Radios & Televisions
description_html:
A ham radio logbook with room to write.

Most logbooks squeeze tiny rows and waste space on columns you never fill. Good Copy gives every contact a tall row, puts the width where you need it (Name and QTH/grid), and records rig, power and antenna once per page instead of on every line.

  • 60 log pages: 1,320 contacts
  • Columns: date, UTC, frequency/band, mode, call, RST sent, RST rcvd, name, QTH/grid, QSL sent/received, notes
  • Extra-wide inner margin so you never write into the spine
  • 6 POTA / SOTA activation logs with park-to-park and summit-to-summit notes
  • 4 contest logs and 4 net logs
  • Worked All States, DXCC (162 entries) and grid-square trackers
  • QSL card log, station, antenna and memory-channel records
  • Quick reference: US band edges, FT8 and calling frequencies, phonetic alphabet, Q-codes, RST scale, UTC conversion

8.5 x 11 inches, 100 pages. A practical gift for new licensees and seasoned operators.

Not affiliated with the ARRL, POTA or SOTA.
research: 24 Nov 2026: sellers are 8.5x11. ARRL logbook BSR 39.7k (brand), indie 134.9k (120pp, 2019), 225.8k (108pp), POTA pocket 351k. Critical reviews: rows too small, doubled RST columns + wide power column waste space, no room for name/QTH, won't lie flat, cover logo mimicked ARRL. Title 'Good Copy' unused in the niche.
